items.stem:
Zoya, Sneha and Karthik are partners in Pillai Brothers, Coimbatore. Karthik has become permanently incapable of performing the duties of a partner and Zoya wants the firm closed, while Sneha wants to continue with a new partner.
(i) Can the firm be dissolved by the court on this ground? Name the mode. (ii) If Zoya and Sneha continue with a new partner instead, is it dissolution of partnership or of the firm? Why?
items.answer: (i) Yes: dissolution by court on permanent incapacity of a partner. (ii) Dissolution of partnership (reconstitution): the business continues under a new agreement.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Yes: dissolution by court on permanent incapacity of a partner. (ii) Dissolution of partnership (reconstitution): the business continues under a new agreement.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about dissolution is correct?

Books are closed on dissolution of partnership.

items.stem:
Goyal Enterprises was formed by Sneha and Ananya for a fixed term of three years to run a trade fair stall in Dehradun. The term has ended but both want to continue for two more years.
(i) What happens to the firm on expiry of the term if they do nothing? (ii) If they continue without a new agreement, what kind of partnership is it?
items.answer: (i) It is dissolved on the happening of a contingency (expiry of the fixed term). (ii) A partnership at will on the same terms, which can later be dissolved by notice.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) It is dissolved on the happening of a contingency (expiry of the fixed term). (ii) A partnership at will on the same terms, which can later be dissolved by notice.

items.stem: Identify the mode of dissolution of the firm. In each case give a reason. (i) A government notification makes the business carried on by Mehta Agencies illegal. (ii) Tara, a partner of Mehta Agencies, has become of unsound mind and another partner files a suit.
items.answer: (i) Compulsory dissolution: The business has become unlawful. (ii) Dissolution by court: The court may order dissolution on a partner's insanity.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Compulsory dissolution"?
items.answer: Dissolution when all or all but one partner become insolvent, or the business becomes illegal.
items.markingKey: (b) Compulsory dissolution: Dissolution when all or all but one partner become insolvent, or the business becomes illegal.
options: Dissolution of a partnership at will when a partner gives written notice of intention to dissolve.

items.stem: Distinguish between dissolution of partnership and dissolution of firm on the basis of settlement of assets and liabilities, court's intervention, termination of business and economic relationship.
items.answer: (i) Settlement of assets and liabilities: dissolution of partnership: assets and liabilities are revalued and a new balance sheet drawn; dissolution of firm: assets are sold and liabilities paid off. (ii) Court's intervention: dissolution of partnership: no court order is needed; dissolution of firm: a firm may be dissolved by order of the court. (iii) Termination of business: dissolution of partnership: business continues; dissolution of firm: business is closed. (iv) Economic relationship: dissolution of partnership: the relationship continues among some partners; dissolution of firm: the relationship ends among all partners.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each basis: (i) Settlement of assets and liabilities: dissolution of partnership: assets and liabilities are revalued and a new balance sheet drawn; dissolution of firm: assets are sold and liabilities paid off. (ii) Court's intervention: dissolution of partnership: no court order is needed; dissolution of firm: a firm may be dissolved by order of the court. (iii) Termination of business: dissolution of partnership: business continues; dissolution of firm: business is closed. (iv) Economic relationship: dissolution of partnership: the relationship continues among some partners; dissolution of firm: the relationship ends among all partners.

items.stem: Explain any four items in the order of payment out of the firm's assets under Section 48.
items.answer: (i) Debts of the firm to third parties: Outside liabilities are paid first. (ii) Advances (loans) by partners: Then each partner is paid rateably what is due for advances as distinct from capital. (iii) Capitals of partners: Then each partner is paid rateably what is due on account of capital. (iv) Residue among partners: Any surplus is divided among partners in their profit-sharing ratio.

(iii) Capitals of partners: Then each partner is paid rateably what is due on account of capital. (iv) Residue among partners: Any surplus is divided among partners in their profit-sharing ratio.
